newsitem.title: USA: HOME INSURANCE PAYS $60 MLN IN NCCI SETTLEMENT.
newsitem.headline: HOME INSURANCE PAYS $60 MLN IN NCCI SETTLEMENT.

text.p: Home Insurance Co agreed to pay $60 million to settle obligations to the National Council on Compensation Insurance, the National Workers Compensation Reinsurance Pool and the National Pool's participating companies, a regulatory representative said.
The obligations had an estimated present value of about $160 million and a future value of about $270 million, said David Nichols, a representative of the New Hampshire insurance department.
This was believed to be the largest of the Home's non-policyholder obligations, he said.
"This was a pretty big thing for them to have resolved," he said. "It was clearly very important for the company to complete this transaction," he said.
New Hampshire regulators placed Home Insurance, the principal subsidiary of Home Holdings Inc, under formal supervision in March because of concern about its capital levels.
Nichols said this settlement was important because the company's surplus had nearly evaporated.
This transaction increases the surplus because the payment will be much less than the obligation that was on the books, he said.
In a statement earlier, Home Holdings said the settlement will save the company $100 million and fully releases Home Insurance's obligations.
Home Insurance is also in settlement talks with other workers compensation pools as well as non-workers compensation pools, Nichols said.
However, he said, "this was clearly the largest pool of that kind that the Home was involved in."
Home Holdings was formerly majority owned by a unit of Trygg-Hansa AB.
